text:
sam: Quick flag from onboarding Peregrine11B-int4. Ran full-latency pass on bookcrawl and saw periodic 6-token collapse after ~3.3k tokens. Not a complete loop but strong degeneracy.

rita: which tokenizer was used? Peregrine started life with gemma-spm but we tried qwen-bpe mapping right?

sam: exactly. pipeline: peregrine_base -> quant-int4. Tokenizer: qwen-bpe-v3 remapped via our vocab-packer. Seq=len 4096, temp=0.0 greedy sampling to stress.

hao: any quick token id dump at collapse window?

sam: snippet (ids at collapse):
```
[210, 421, 210, 421, 210, 421]
```
repeating two-id motif, then collapses into short repeating clause.

zane: that smells like aliasing in the remap table. But also remember Peregrine used a heterogenous rotary scheme: early layers use per-head freqs, later layers use global scaled freqs. Mixed schemes + aggressive quantization can introduce phase misalignment.

ci-bot: queued quick-eval: eval_runner --model peregrine11b_int4 --task bookcrawl --seq 4096 --runs 6

ci-bot: quick-eval results: 5/6 runs show collapse onset between 3208-3340. Perplexity jumps and top-k token distribution tightens.

rita: let's run two experiments: (1) keep rotary tables and kv accumulation as fp32 during decode, (2) disable vocab-packer remap to use original ids. We can run in parallel.

hao: also add a third experiment: convert rotary frequency tables using alternative scaling transform we used for mistral-to-llm conversions (scale factor alpha=0.997). Might stabilize phase accumulation.

sam: starting them now. Commands:
```
# A: numeric-safe
python infra/run_infer.py --model peregrine11b_int4 --rotary-fp32 --kv-accum-fp32 --seq 4096
# B: raw tokenizer
python infra/run_infer.py --model peregrine11b_int4 --tokenizer-override raw:preserve_ids --seq 4096
# C: adjusted freq scale
python infra/run_infer.py --model peregrine11b_int4 --rotary-scale-alpha 0.997 --seq 4096
```

ci-bot: run A finished: collapse eliminated in 6/6 quick runs, runtime +5.1%.

ci-bot: run B finished: collapse delayed but still present in 3/6 runs, onset ~3600, repeating id motif reduced.

ci-bot: run C finished: partial improvement, collapse onset moved to ~3450 on average, not eliminated.

rita: interpretation: numeric precision on rotary accumulation is primary root cause; tokenizer remap aggravates by introducing alias tokens which get amplified. Alpha tweak helps but not sufficient.

hao: follow-ups: (1) change quant packer to avoid folding rotary constants to int8; store as bf16 or reserve 16-bit for per-head multipliers, (2) add validator that checks remap uniqueness for control and zero-width characters, (3) add a long-sequence synthetic to nightly CI that looks for short repeating-id motifs.

sam: I'll open PRs. Draft notes: Peregrine11B-int4 advisory - keep rotary constants at higher precision until packer change lands. Also add an onboarding checklist entry to verify mixed-rotary architectures during conversion.

zane: add perf impact doc for product - latency hit and mitigation path (progressive FP32 fallback for only rotary+kv).

rita: tagging infra/bench for nightly job. cc @customer-signal in case any early customers see weird long-story outputs.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll link PRs once ready. :white_check_mark:
